messages:
kevin: fyi customer reported negative tokens/sec in console for several routes after they paused ingestion for ~12m. billing mismatch too. screenshot attached :grimacing:
maria-ops: ugh. which customer + which time window? can you paste the console link and the graph time range?
kevin: ACME Corp. dashboard link: https://console.redwood/acme/metrics (redacted). window 2024-06-20T13:12 -> 13:28 UTC. they paused their forwarders at 13:15 and resumed at 13:27. attached small GIF.
ajay: putting up quick raw-counter query from streaming ingesters to see the delta:```promql
sum by(route) (increase(streaming.tokens_total[5m]))
```
ajay: also checking rollup logs for that interval:```
2024-06-20T13:15:02Z rollup: consumer paused partition=12
2024-06-20T13:15:13Z rollup: window_end=2024-06-20T13:15:00 emitted
2024-06-20T13:27:45Z rollup: consumer resumed partition=12
2024-06-20T13:28:00Z rollup: computed delta=-482 for route=/v1/generate
```
emily: negative delta usually means out-of-order window or counter reset. did the ingesters restart and reset their counters?
kevin: customer says they paused forwarders gracefully, no process restart. log snippets show gap only.
maria-ops: @ajay can you check consumer offsets for that partition and whether there was a replay/backfill that overlapped windows? also check if kv-cache or prefix caching emitted synthetic zeroes.
ajay: offsets look continuous, no seek. but I see the rollup service emitted a non-monotonic counter read when the consumer resumed: raw counter value decreased by ~600 vs last seen. likely a transient counter wrap or exporter restart.
sre-bot: automated note: a single negative rollup delta triggered at 2024-06-20T13:28:00 for route=/v1/generate. alert suppressed due to maintenance window.
emily: short repro steps for oncall: 1) pause forwarder for a partition for ~10-15m 2) resume 3) watch rollup calc for that partition 3) query raw consumer offsets + metrics.
kevin: customer is asking for billing credit because tokens/sec dip produced negative billed tokens in that interval. we need to explain and have a remediation.
maria-ops: remediation plan: (a) clamp negative deltas to 0 at rollup emit (b) schedule a targeted replay/backfill for the affected time windows to regenerate correct rollups (c) detect exporter restarts and annotate windows so we ignore risky deltas for billing.
ajay: I can push a hotfix to rollup service to guard against negative deltas (simple if delta < 0 -> set to 0 and tag as "clamped"). will add metric rollup.clamped_count so we can audit.
emily: for the customer: propose refund for that billing interval and follow-up with them once backfill completes. include short postmortem.
kevin: ack. I'll open billing ticket and request refund. timeline: ajay to land hotfix today, backfill job queued for tomorrow 03:00 UTC for the affected partitions.
support-bot: ticket created: SB-14287 linked to this thread.
maria-ops: follow-ups: please include the replay plan in the support ticket with timeframe and add dashboard that surfaces "clamped" rollups so customers can see it. also create alert that fires if clamped_count > 0 for >1m (to catch noisy exporters).
ajay: pushing pr now: https://git.redwood/rollup/merge_requests/523 (hotfix + unit tests). will notify when deployed.
kevin: thanks all. keeping ACME updated. will post resolution when backfill finished. :thumbsup:
